readiness_words: Checklist items are open: StackToIT lists the work and counts an item done only when the customer marks it in the decisions file (application_checklists); StackToIT never deploys the application.
validation_scope: A kubeconform check or a kubectl apply --dry-run of the manifest establishes YAML validity only, not behaviour: it accepts a REQUIRED_ token in a string field, an empty ConfigMap and a Secret that does not exist, and runs nothing; the checklist of the application compatibility contract and an application smoke test on the target are what show that the workload works.

containers.name: ui-service
containers.image_rebinding: pulled from where the source pulls it (Amazon ECR image public.ecr.aws/aws-containers/retail-store-sample-ui:1.6.3): decide where the images live on STACKIT, that the cluster can reach the registry, and the pull secret
probes: livenessProbe: exec curl -f http://localhost:8080/actuator/health (the ECS health check)
startupProbe: the same check over the start period

endpoints.source: ui:80 (the Service Connect alias of port ui-service in the namespace not visible statically)
endpoints.target: ui:80 (the Kubernetes Service ui, port 80 → container port 8080, in the namespace the manifests are applied into)
endpoints.work: the Kubernetes Service keeps the name and port the clients call: check that they resolve it from their namespace; the Service Connect proxy (its retries, timeouts, TLS and metrics) is not carried

endpoints.source: a load balancer target group → container not visible statically port not visible statically
endpoints.target: the NodePort Service ui-nodeport (node port 30000 → container port 8080), the target pool of stackit_application_load_balancer.retail_app_ecs_alb_this at the private IPs of the cluster's nodes
endpoints.work: set the node IPs of the target pool (an input of the load balancer) and keep them current as the node pool changes, or answer the decision DEC-GEN-DEC-GEN-CONVERT-INGRESS-EXPOSURE-PATH-ALIAS-CONVERT-MOD-06557BC6 (aws.ingress.exposure-path) with another exposure path

identity.target: open: the decision target.workload.identity (inputs.json) chooses federated_service_account (a Kubernetes ServiceAccount federated to the STACKIT service account of the role), service_account_key (a key of that service account mounted as a Secret) or no_workload_identity
identity.work: answer target.workload.identity for module.retail_app_ecs.module.ui_service.aws_ecs_service.this; until then the pods run with no identity and every call the application made with the task role module.retail_app_ecs.module.ui_service.aws_iam_role.task_role fails
manual_steps: answer the input target.workload.identity for module.retail_app_ecs.module.ui_service.aws_ecs_service.this in inputs.json: with federated_service_account the draft writes the stackit_service_account of module.retail_app_ecs.module.ui_service.aws_iam_role.task_role, its federated identity provider for the SKE cluster's service-account issuer and the Kubernetes ServiceAccount ui in the manifest

until then, create a STACKIT service account named after the task role module.retail_app_ecs.module.ui_service.aws_iam_role.task_role and grant it the role assignments the policies of module.retail_app_ecs.module.ui_service.aws_iam_role.task_role give (identity.tf lists them as the architect's variable)

federate it to the SKE cluster's service-account issuer for the subject system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:ui, and apply the ServiceAccount of applications/ui.templates.yaml (its annotation holds the service account's e-mail) in the namespace of the workload

change the application from the AWS SDK credential chain to the STACKIT SDK, which picks up the projected token: every call the application made with module.retail_app_ecs.module.ui_service.aws_iam_role.task_role fails until it does

dns_dependencies.name: ui
dns_dependencies.source: a Service Connect alias in the Cloud Map private DNS namespace retailstore.local (module.retail_app_ecs.aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace.this): the clients of the namespace resolve it through the Service Connect proxy of their tasks
dns_dependencies.target: ui.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local (the Kubernetes Service ui; ui from a pod of the same namespace)
dns_dependencies.verification: resolve, from a pod of a client of ui, ui and ui.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local: expect the ClusterIP of the Kubernetes Service ui (kubectl get service ui)

checklist.subject: module.retail_app_ecs.module.ui_service.aws_iam_role.task_role
checklist.work: answer target.workload.identity for module.retail_app_ecs.module.ui_service.aws_ecs_service.this; until then the pods run with no identity and every call the application made with the task role module.retail_app_ecs.module.ui_service.aws_iam_role.task_role fails

checklist.subject: ui
checklist.work: run an application smoke test on the target: the pods start, answer their clients through the Kubernetes Service ui, reach every dependency above and read and write their data; StackToIT runs nothing on the target
